activity: Hands-on cooking classes (pasta and other cuisines)
how: Hands-on cooking classes cover pasta and ravioli (2e, 4e), Japanese, Vietnamese and Thai cuisine in many arrondissements.
Paris tea schools and shops run Japanese tea ceremony (chanoyu) demonstrations with hands-on bowl preparation, e.g. Takamatsu Somi sessions and Maison Jugetsudo sencha workshops.
Barista and latte art workshops are offered in Paris 9e and 10e, alongside coffee tasting and caffeology classes.

A 2-hour sake history, production and tasting workshop is listed in Paris 16e (tasting, not brewing); Wakaze, a Paris sake brewery founded in 2019, produces locally but public brewing courses are unconfirmed.
Sake tasting workshops with an expert run at the Caves du Louvre (7 sakes with food pairings) and at a Paris 16e venue via Funbooker.
A baker in Paris 12e runs a 2.5-hour sourdough bread workshop (rue Montgallet) where participants shape and bake loaves and take them home.
venue: Atelier pain au levain, rue Montgallet

how: Sushi workshops with tasting are held in Paris 6e (traditional sushi) and at Le Labo Culinaire (17e).
Guided whisky tastings are sold in Paris by Pro Degustation (9e), La Compagnie du mieux boire (11e) and Maison Benjamin Kuentz (7e), with shops such as La Maison du Whisky running tastings.
Whisky tasting workshops and blending sessions run in Paris (Atelier assemblage de whisky in the 7th, whisky tastings in the 11th, whisky and chocolate pairings in the 1st), from about 49 EUR.
Oenology courses and guided wine tastings run at Les Caves du Louvre and other Paris venues, including a 4-hour level 1 tasting course.
LPO members lead a free guided bird walk in the Bois de Boulogne every Sunday morning (running since 1946), beginners welcome; the Bois de Vincennes has a bird reserve with observation hides.
venue: LPO Ile-de-France, Bois de Boulogne walk

how: The City of Paris' free monthly nature programme (Maison Paris Nature at the Parc Floral and others) offers guided walks and workshops on wild fauna and flora, with insects as occasional themes.
The Société française de numismatique holds monthly public-interest sessions for coin and medal enthusiasts at the BnF Département des Monnaies, médailles et antiques.
venue: Société française de numismatique, BnF Richelieu

how: Specialist comics shops such as Album Comics on Boulevard Saint-Germain and Comics Records in the Marais sell new and back-issue comics for collectors.
The Saphir'Art geology and mineralogy association (Sceaux) held a mineral and fossil exhibition and sale in Chambourcy; the FFAMP federation lists affiliated clubs.
Collector sneaker resale shops such as Larry Deadstock in the Marais and StockX Paris, plus periodic Sneakers Event Paris fairs and auctions, serve sneaker collectors.
Rue Drouot in Paris 9e hosts many philatelist dealers' shops serving stamp collectors.
Specialist shops sell vintage toys and collectors' figurines, such as Lulu Berlu (60 years of figurines) and Au Plat d'Etain (toy soldiers since 1775).
Specialist shops such as MEiSiA (Paris 10e) host Pokemon TCG events and tournaments, and the Royaume du TCG convention is held at Paris Nord Villepinte.
Independent record shops such as Dizonord (rue André-Messager, Paris 18e) sell vinyl; the City of Paris subsidises record shops among cultural businesses.
Collectors buy and trade vintage watches through Paris dealers, Collector Square and Hotel Drouot auctions, though no regular club or bourse was found.
Paris is inland on the Seine; the nearest whale and dolphin watching is on the Atlantic coast (Brittany), roughly 4-5 hours away.
The Archives nationales operate reading rooms at Pierrefitte-sur-Seine and in Paris (Marais) plus an online virtual reading room with about 31,000 inventories.
The Louvre, Centre Pompidou (with Cezanne et nous at the Grand Palais) and many other galleries and art museums show ongoing exhibitions in Paris.
Dozens of French- and English-language book clubs meet in Paris (e.g. English-speaking Book Club in Paris, Paris Great Books Club, Club de lecture Les Mots Passants), several events per week.
Writing workshops and sessions run across Paris (Paris Lit Up Right Bank Writers' Group, Libre d'ecrire, Ecrivaines Parisiennes Sunday atelier, Ready-Set-Write) in French and English.
Centre Paris Anim' Beaujon runs an eloquence (public speaking) workshop for teens and adults, which covers speaking skills rather than formal competitive debate.
The Institut du monde arabe hosts a museum, exhibitions, talks, film and music events and Arabic language courses.
The Archives de Paris (Paris 19e) hold over 13 million digitised pages of genealogical sources (civil registers etc.) searchable online and on site.
Many guided walking tours of Paris (Paris peu frequentable, Paris du crime, street-art in the Butte-aux-Cailles, Montmartre drawing walk) can be booked.
venue: Visite guidee Le Paris du crime

how: Weekly language-exchange meetups run in Paris bars and cafes (Denfert Polyglottes, Afterwork Paris, Paris Multi-Language Meetup, ChitChat) for French, English, Japanese, Korean, Italian and more.
The Alliance Française Paris Île-de-France runs in-person and online French courses at all levels plus workshops at its school on Boulevard Raspail.
The Goethe-Institut Paris (av. d'Iena) runs German courses from A1 for adults, teens and children, in person and online.
The Maison de la culture du Japon a Paris offers Japanese-language courses (IRODORI programme, JLPT information) alongside a tadoku reading salon.
venue: Maison de la culture du Japon a Paris (MCJP)

how: The Korean Cultural Centre in Paris offers Korean language courses (in person at the King Sejong Institute and online) plus calligraphy and paper-craft workshops.
IVT (International Visual Theatre) training centre teaches LSF (French Sign Language) courses for beginners and advanced learners, about 1,000 trainees a year.
The Instituto Cervantes Paris (rue Quentin Bauchart, 8e) runs Spanish courses by semester with a placement test and online enrolment.
INALCO teaches modern Tamil (licence, master, and as a minor or language option) in Paris.
Paris has hundreds of museums, from the Louvre (with a Zurbaran retrospective running into 2027) to the Centre Pompidou and city museums, many with timed ticketing.
FUN MOOC, the French national platform, hosts free online university courses from French institutions; Paris universities and grandes écoles contribute many.
Cafe philo discussion evenings run in Paris, including Groupe Meetup Paris Philosophie (Sunday cafe philo) and a weekly English-language Cosy Cave Conversations cafe philo in the 10th.
venue: Cosy Cave Conversations (Cafe Philo in English)

how: Paris Lit Up runs a weekly Thursday open mic, and the Paris Poetry Circle holds English-language poetry readings in bars.
The College de France gives free public lectures open to all on a first-come basis (arrive about 30 minutes early), mostly at the Marcelin-Berthelot site.
The Cite des sciences et de l'industrie (Universcience) in La Villette runs permanent and temporary science exhibitions, a Cite des enfants and a planetarium.
venue: Cite des sciences et de l'industrie

how: The City of Paris promotes self-guided heritage routes, such as the Libération de Paris trail (from the Hôtel de Ville to the Musée de la Libération) on foot or by bike via the Détour app, and the Parcours Mémori.elles.
Many Toastmasters clubs meet in Paris (Lutece 75, Les Ailes in Paris 8, Paris La Defense, Forum des Rives de Seine), mostly weekly evening meetings in French or English.
The Musee de la Liberation de Paris - Musee du General Leclerc - Musee Jean Moulin covers the Liberation of Paris in WWII, with free permanent collections and the Rol-Tanguy command post.
venue: Musee de la Liberation de Paris

how: SPA shelters near Paris (e.g. Gennevilliers) and associations such as Reves de Chiens (Viry-Chatillon) recruit volunteers; the SPA also seeks volunteer investigators in Paris.

There is no sea coast, but river and lake clean-ups run in the Paris area, e.g. litter-collecting kayak outings at the Île de loisirs de Créteil (18 Oct) and the City of Paris Ménage ton canal campaign.
Paris Ice Club (Paris 9e) sells guided Wim Hof-method breathing and ice-bath sessions at 4-10 C, and a cryotherapy cold bath is bookable in Paris 17e.
The City of Paris supports a network of jardins partagés (shared community gardens) run by residents' associations, with guidance on joining or creating one.
Paris provides fenced off-leash dog areas (canisites/parcs canins), e.g. a dedicated dog park opened in the 10e arrondissement.
Paris has large Meetup communities plus friend-making platforms such as Frimake that organise interest-based outings among strangers.
Massage, scrubs and hammam packages (Thai massage in the 12th, hammam-gommage-massage in the 13th and 17th) and sound massage sessions are bookable across Paris.
Group meditation sessions run in Paris, e.g. Muraqaba silent Sufi meditation, Heartfulness meditation, and free Sahaj meditation in the 17th.
Nos Quartiers ont du Talent (NQT) and Frateli run mentoring programmes pairing professionals with young graduates and students, active in the Paris region.
No natural hot springs exist in the Paris basin; the nearest thermal-spring resorts are several hours away (e.g. Bourbonne-les-Bains, Haute-Marne, about 3.5 hours).
A Japanese-style spa with private indoor pool at a 19th-century hotel in the 2nd arrondissement; no natural hot-spring onsen exists.

Culture Parkour and other associations hold parkour classes in the covered Centr'Halles Park at Forum des Halles; Pink Parkour runs an adult evening class and the city offers free introductory sessions.
The SPA shelter in Gennevilliers (RER C) is the nearest to Paris and handles dog and cat adoptions with ID and address documents, plus a Maison des Chats in the Marais.
Pilates classes run in Paris studios (e.g. The Pilates Project, which also hosts yoga classes) and as Meetup pilates sessions such as Pilates & Girls Talk.
Paris municipal Centre Paris Anim' (e.g. Beaujon, Musidora, Bessie Smith) run weekly adult Qi Gong classes, among over 100 listed sessions.
Social running groups meet weekly in Paris and nearby (Paris Running Club beginner runs along the Seine, Founders Running Club Paris, La Team Fit Rueil, Paris Hash House Harriers).

Public and private saunas in Paris and inner suburbs, including hotel spas (Hotel Este, 10e), private infrared saunas (13e), a Japanese sauna (2e) and spa-sauna-hammam sites in Vitry-sur-Seine and Romainville; sessions from about 18 EUR.
Alcoholics Anonymous France runs a searchable directory of in-person and online meetings, including in Paris and Ile-de-France.
Association Atout Chine (Paris 5e) runs a weekly all-levels tai chi workshop, and Paris Anim' centres, the Chinese Cultural Centre and Kordiane (14e) offer adult tai chi classes.
The Pagoda of the Bois de Vincennes (Paris 12e), seat of the Union bouddhiste de France, is a working Buddhist temple housing Europe's tallest Buddha statue.
The official Catacombes of Paris route and guided small-group visits give legal access to part of the underground quarries, while wider urban exploration is illegal.
JeVeuxAider.gouv.fr lists thousands of volunteer missions in Paris (Secours populaire, Serve the City Paris, Protection civile Paris Seine and others).
Many yoga studios and workshops in Paris and nearby (kitten yoga, parent-child yoga, face yoga, pilates/yoga in infrared sauna) bookable per session; classes from about 25 EUR on Funbooker.
No cliffs or tall natural exits in the Paris area and jumping from structures is illegal; the nearest sites are the Alps (about 6 hours) or Normandy cliffs (about 2.5 hours).
Bullfighting is not practised in the Paris region; corridas are held only in southern France (Nimes, Arles, Bayonne), roughly 6-8 hours away.
A 'Benji ejection' reverse bungee at the Cergy-Pontoise leisure island catapults riders to treetop height in under 2 seconds; no conventional bungee jump from a bridge or tower was found.
venue: Ile de loisirs de Cergy-Pontoise (Benji ejection)

how: The Cergy-Pontoise leisure island has an 820 m cable tow (teleski nautique) for water skiing and wakeboarding with obstacle modules, from about EUR 9.
venue: Ile de loisirs de Cergy-Pontoise (teleski nautique)

how: The Paris region has no gorges or canyon rivers; the nearest canyoning is in the Alps, Pyrenees or Vosges, roughly 4-8 hours away.
No flooded natural cave systems near Paris; the nearest cave-diving regions are the Lot/Ardeche karst areas, roughly 6-8 hours away.
Only the Catacombs of Paris ossuary section of the former quarries is open to visitors (Paris Musees, Denfert-Rochereau); the wider tunnel network is closed to the public.
Needs reliable snow and mountain terrain; the nearest options are in the Alps or Vosges, roughly 5-6 hours from Paris.
No glaciers in the Paris region; the nearest is the Mer de Glace at Chamonix, about 6 hours away by train and road.
Accrobranche at the Cergy-Pontoise leisure island has 12 aerial courses of rope bridges, nets and ziplines over the lakes, for ages 6 and up (shorter courses) and 1.50 m and up (harder ones).
Aerokart in Argenteuil (about 20 minutes from Paris) runs a free-fall wind-tunnel simulator alongside its indoor karting and escape game.
Crazy Park in Bonneuil-sur-Marne has the Ile-de-France region's only year-round indoor ski simulator, and temporary snow and luge slopes appear in winter.
Alpine luge/toboggan runs need mountain slopes; the nearest are in the Vosges or Alps, roughly 5-6 hours from Paris.
No high mountains in the Paris basin; the nearest alpine mountaineering is Chamonix (Mont Blanc massif), about 6 hours away by TGV and road.
Tandem skydives from aerodromes around the region such as Meaux, Cesson, Pontoise and La Ferté-Gaucher; none within Paris itself.
Tandem paragliding baptisms by winch launch around Évry (Essonne) and Bassevelle (Seine-et-Marne); the region is flat, so no ridge soaring.
No free-roaming large African wildlife in the Paris region; the nearest wildlife park drives are about 45 km out (Thoiry) and real safaris are in Africa.
No desert or large dunes near Paris; the nearest big dune is the Dune du Pilat near Arcachon (about 6 hours by train/road) and true desert is in North Africa.
Indoor ski slope on an inclined conveyor belt with instructors, 30-minute sessions, gear provided, ages six and up.
No snow-reliable mountains near Paris; the nearest resorts are the Vosges (about 5 hours) and the Alps such as Chamonix (about 6 hours).
No active or ash-slope volcano in the Paris region; volcano boarding is done at sites such as Cerro Negro in Nicaragua, with the nearest French volcanic range (Auvergne) about 4 hours away.
The Cergy-Pontoise leisure island has an artificial whitewater river with waterfalls, obstacles and adjustable current for guided rafting, on reservation; natural-river rafting is far away.
venue: Ile de loisirs de Cergy-Pontoise (stade d'eau vive)

how: Every course at the Cergy-Pontoise accrobranche includes ziplines, some over 200 m above the lake with speeds above 50 km/h.
